sections.section_name: Section A - Objective Type / MCQs / Assertion-Reasoning

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the standard SI unit used worldwide to measure length?
questions.answer: C) Metre

questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements labeled as Assertion (A) and Reason (R):
Assertion (A): We must include roughage (dietary fiber) in our daily diet.
Reason (R): Roughage helps in the easy movement of undigested food through the digestive tract.
Choose the correct option:
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
C) A is true but R is false.
D) A is false but R is true.
questions.answer: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.question_text: Which of the following materials is generally considered opaque?
questions.answer: B) Wooden board

questions.question_text: What type of motion is exhibited by the spinning blades of a ceiling fan?

questions.question_text: Why do we need a standard unit of measurement, like the metre, instead of using handspans? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Handspans vary from person to person, causing inaccurate and inconsistent measurements. A standard unit like the metre ensures exact, uniform measurements worldwide.

questions.question_text: Name the two poles of a magnet and state the fundamental law of magnetic attraction. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The two poles are the North pole and the South pole. The fundamental law states that opposite poles attract each other, while like poles repel each other.

questions.question_text: List any two ways to test if a given food item contains starch. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: To test for starch, add a few drops of dilute iodine solution to the food item. If the color changes to blue-black, starch is present.

questions.question_text: Define 'translucent' materials and give one common everyday example. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Translucent materials allow only a portion of light to pass through them, making objects on the other side appear blurred. Butter paper is a common example.

questions.question_text: State two specific adaptations that help a fish survive easily in an aquatic habitat. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Fish have a streamlined body shape that reduces water resistance while swimming, and they possess gills that allow them to extract dissolved oxygen from water.

questions.question_text: Identify the type of motion shown by a plucked guitar string and explain briefly why. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A plucked guitar string shows oscillatory motion because it vibrates, rapidly moving back and forth across its mean resting position.

questions.question_text: Explain the step-by-step process of how you would make a temporary compass using a magnetized iron needle, a cork, and a cup of water. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Insert a magnetized iron needle horizontally through a small piece of cork. Float the cork in a cup filled with water. The cork will rotate freely, and the needle will align itself to point steadily in the North-South direction.

questions.question_text: A student walked 2.5 kilometers from her house to the school and then walked back. Calculate the total distance traveled in meters. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The one-way distance is 2.5 km. Since 1 kilometer equals 1000 meters, 2.5 km is 2500 meters. The total round trip is 2500 meters to school plus 2500 meters back, equaling a total distance of 5000 meters.

questions.question_text: Differentiate between autotrophs and heterotrophs based on their mode of obtaining food, providing one specific example for each category. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Autotrophs are living organisms that can synthesize their own food using sunlight through photosynthesis, for example, a mango tree. Heterotrophs cannot produce their own food and depend on plants or other animals for nutrition, for example, a lion.

questions.question_text: Describe a simple school experiment to demonstrate that light travels in a straight line, using three cardboard pieces with holes. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Align three square cardboard pieces vertically with a small hole punched in the exact center of each. Place a lighted candle behind the last hole. You can only see the flame when all three holes are in a perfect straight line.

questions.question_text: Explain why it is highly dangerous to rely solely on junk food, even though it provides energy. Relate your answer to a balanced diet. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Junk food provides high energy mostly from fats and sugars but completely lacks essential nutrients like vitamins, minerals, and roughage. A balanced diet requires all nutrients in the right proportions to prevent severe deficiency diseases and maintain long-term organ health.

questions.question_text: You are given a mixture of iron filings and sawdust. Explain how you would effectively separate them, naming the specific property utilized. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Spread the mixture on paper and pass a strong bar magnet over it. The iron filings will immediately attract and stick to the magnet. This utilizes the magnetic property of iron, leaving the non-magnetic sawdust behind.

questions.question_text: While measuring the length of a pencil, your ruler is broken at the zero mark. How will you take an accurate measurement? Explain with an example. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Place one end of the pencil at a clear, unbroken mark, such as the 2 cm mark. Record the reading at the other end, for instance, 10 cm. Subtract the starting mark from the final reading (10 - 2 = 8 cm) for the accurate length.

questions.question_text: How do camels adapt to survive the harsh, dry conditions of a desert? Mention at least three specific physiological adaptations. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Camels have long legs to keep their bodies away from hot sand. They can drink large quantities of water at once and store it. They excrete very little urine, and their dung is completely dry, helping them minimize water loss efficiently.

questions.question_text:
Case Study: During a physical education class, a student feels extremely weak, dizzy, and is diagnosed with anemia by the school nurse. Later, another student complains of bleeding gums and slow-healing wounds. 
Analyze both situations. Identify the specific nutrient deficiencies causing these distinct symptoms, name the diseases, and recommend two food sources for each student to cure their conditions. [60-80 words]
questions.answer: The first student has Anemia, caused by a severe deficiency of Iron. To cure this, they should eat iron-rich foods like spinach, apples, or liver. The second student is suffering from Scurvy, caused by a lack of Vitamin C, which leads to bleeding gums. To treat scurvy, they must urgently consume citrus fruits like amla (Indian gooseberry), oranges, and lemons. A balanced diet prevents both diseases.

questions.question_text:
Case Study: Ravi tied a strong magnet to a toy car and tried to push another identical toy car holding a magnet. He observed that sometimes the second car moved away without being touched, and sometimes they forcefully crashed together.
Explain the scientific principles behind Ravi's observations. How can this magnetic force property be applied in modern transportation systems? [60-80 words]
questions.answer: Ravi observed magnetic repulsion and attraction. When the like poles (e.g., North and North) faced each other, the magnetic force repelled, pushing the second car away without physical contact. When opposite poles faced each other, they attracted and crashed. This principle of magnetic repulsion (levitation) is utilized in modern Maglev (magnetic levitation) trains, allowing them to float above the tracks and travel at ultra-high speeds without friction.

questions.question_text: Discuss the classification of objects based on transparency. Define transparent, translucent, and opaque materials, providing two examples of each. Why is this classification useful in daily life, such as in building construction? [60-80 words]
questions.answer: Materials are classified by how light passes through them. Transparent objects (clear glass, pure water) allow light to pass completely, letting us see clearly. Translucent objects (frosted glass, butter paper) allow partial light passage, creating blurred vision. Opaque objects (wood, metals) block light entirely, forming dark shadows. In construction, this is crucial: we use transparent glass for windows to let in sunlight, translucent glass in bathrooms for privacy, and opaque bricks for walls to block weather and sight.

questions.question_text: Explain the structural hierarchy of living organisms starting from the cellular level. Mention the five defining characteristics that strictly separate a living organism from a non-living object like a stone. [60-80 words]
questions.answer: The structural hierarchy begins with the cell, the basic unit of life. Similar cells group to form tissues; tissues form organs; organs coordinate to create organ systems, which together build the complete organism. The five defining characteristics of living things are: 1) Need for food and nutrition. 2) Growth and development over time. 3) Respiration (breathing and energy release). 4) Response to external stimuli. 5) Reproduction (producing offspring). A non-living stone exhibits none of these life processes.
